doc.title: Ametria Dock interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 4, 2019

chapter: Church upbringing and singing on the spot
title: Being called to sing on the spot in church; set lists and starting the song
summary: Dock was always put on the spot to sing solos, so she made set lists from childhood; church musicians play by ear and follow her lead and riffs.

story.theme_name: Church, faith and religion in a musician's life
story.community_name: Church, faith and jazz: the sacred and the secular

blocks.x: There’s a lot of spontaneity in the presentation of that, right, every Sunday?
So that concept of doing things on the fly was sort of built into you.

Yeah. From early childhood like they had a guest speaker come in. My nickname is Mimi, and so my dad would say, “Mimi come on down.” You know there was no prep. You know. So I’ve been making lists of my favorite songs since I was a kid. And that was helpful for me. I did it because I loved to do it, just to have, so I call it a “set list.” I’ve been making set lists for myself since I was a kid, because I was always put on the spot. And you know, I’m sure anyone wants to just be prepared or ready and so I would practice not just because I wanted to be ready, but because I loved singing. But I was actually putting the work in to be prepared for whatever. It never failed anywhere I went, any church that we would go and visit I was always, always — I would be in the back of the church and they would call me to the front and I would have to sing a solo.
Would you have to sing it in the key that they were going to play it in, or did you get to like suggest?
So a lot of times, most times, some of the black church you have most of the musicians play by ear. So they’re going to follow. So I would start.

Oh yeah. I would start it and they would follow. And so, much like last night, and it just brought me back to my childhood, but yes, it would most of the time be like — or I would say I’m going to sing a particular song and if they knew me and knew the keys that I sang in they would put me in the keys.
Okay. And the concept of then spinning off that song with some riffs and so forth, that was like natural.

Yeah, yeah. And most times again, black church, black musicians, they are accustomed to that style of singing and so they know, you know, you’re going to go off and they’re going to follow you, they’re going to follow where you go.
